title: Why Saffron Costs More Than Any Spice On Earth
note: The queued story saffron-red-gold-myth, made as the third 3D short. One number at most per beat; the closing says why you care. Every claim is in 'sources' with the source's own wording.
lines: Saffron costs more than any spice on Earth, and it's all picked by hand.
Each purple crocus holds just three tiny red threads. You need a whole basket of flowers for one pinch.
Every flower is picked by hand, then every thread is pulled out by hand, for hours on end.
And it's a race. The flowers open at dawn and start to wilt as the day goes on.
That tiny jar isn't pricey for the spice. You're paying for the hands. Would you pay it?

sources.says: At US$5,000 per kg or higher, saffron has long been the world's costliest spice by weight.

sources.claim: It is picked by hand; the price comes from the labour
sources.says: The high retail value of saffron is maintained on world markets because of labour-intensive harvesting methods. Forty hours of labour are needed to pick 150,000 flowers.

sources.claim: Each crocus holds three red threads (stigmas)
sources.says: a style ... branches into three ... Each prong terminates with a vivid crimson stigma

sources.claim: A basket of flowers for one pinch (about 150 flowers per gram)
sources.says: roughly 150 flowers yield 1 g (1/32 oz) of dry saffron threads

sources.claim: The flowers open at dawn and wilt as the day goes on
sources.says: after blossoming at dawn, flowers quickly wilt as the day passes. All plants bloom within a window of one or two weeks.

sets_why: the shop where you pay, the field where it grows, the room where the threads come out, the field at dawn, back to the shop
ideas: a pile of cash for one tiny jar
one flower gives up just three red threads
the clock spins through the hours as he plucks
one flower dies in seconds right in front of us
the tiny jar balances a heap of flowers
storyboard: 1 hook (store): Data behind a low wooden table in the store holds ONE tiny glass jar of red saffron threads up beside his face to us; he sets it down on the table and shoves a big brick of banknote stacks across the table toward it, then a second brick: a wide heap of money next to one tiny jar; he looks back at us, surprised.

2 threads (crocus_field): waist-up in the field, Data holds ONE crocus in front of his chest and with his other hand pulls its three red threads out one at a time, each up into clear air, keeping them fanned in his fingers; he ends holding up all three and looks at us, amazed: one whole flower, three threads.

3 by hand (sorting_room): behind a farmhouse table heaped with purple flowers, Data takes flower after flower in one hand and pulls its red threads into a small dish with the other, faster and faster, the spent flowers landing on a pile on his right; on the wall behind him a clock's hands spin round and the window goes from day to night.

4 race (crocus_field): low among the flowers at dawn: one big open crocus close to the camera, up against the sky, wilts brown and flops over in seconds; Data stands behind it watching, then looks up at us, alarmed.

5 payoff (store): close on the store table: a big brass balance stands right in front of Data, the tiny jar of red saffron alone on its left pan, which sits low; Data lifts his full basket, tips it over the right pan and a stream of purple flowers falls onto it, heaping, and only then does the beam come level; he sets the empty basket down, raises his open hand to us and grins: that's what you pay for.
